questions.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “stage” most nearly mean?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A bar-tailed godwit crossing the Pacific completes the journey in one flight, but a knot travelling the same distance up the Atlantic coast breaks it into three. Each <u>stage</u> ends at an estuary rich enough to let the bird replace the fat it has burned in a fortnight of feeding, and the schedule of the whole journey is set by when those few estuaries are productive.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Willow rods cut in winter can be used in three states. Rods boiled in their own bark for hours take up the tannin in it and come out a warm brown; rods stripped after boiling are cream; rods stripped in spring, when the bark lifts of itself, are white. A basket made from all three shows bands of colour that no dye has touched, so the pattern is a _____ of how each bundle of rods was prepared.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Glasswort grows on the bare mud at the seaward edge of a marsh, where every tide covers it. Salt entering its tissue is not excluded and not excreted; instead the plant takes up water until its stems are swollen and almost translucent, and the salt inside is spread through a far larger volume of sap. The succulence of the plant is therefore a means of _____ rather than a store laid up against drought.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Parchment is not tanned. The skin is soaked in lime, scraped clear of hair and flesh, and then laced to a frame and dried under tension while it is pared thinner. The tension pulls the fibres into layers lying parallel with the surface, and it is that arrangement, not any coating, that gives the sheet its whiteness and its hard writing surface. Drying under strain is therefore _____ to parchment rather than a finishing operation applied to it.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A tower mill grinds only while its sails face the wind, and on an exposed site the wind may back through ninety degrees in an afternoon. Early millers turned the cap by hauling on a tail pole, which meant leaving the stones and going outside. A small wheel set at right angles behind the cap, geared down to the curb it sits on, turns the cap whenever the wind strikes it sideways, so that winding the mill became _____.

questions.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A stone left lying on old pasture sinks. <u>Worms swallow soil at depth and void it at the surface as casts, and a stone resting on the turf is undermined grain by grain as those casts wash down around its edges.</u> Darwin collected and weighed the casts thrown up on measured plots and calculated that the worms of an acre could raise a fifth of an inch of soil in a year. The Roman pavements lying a foot below English grass were buried by nobody.

choices.label: A
choices.content: It reports the quantity of soil the worms of an acre move in a year.

choices.label: B
choices.content: It questions whether the pavements were buried deliberately.

choices.label: C
choices.content: It describes the method by which the casts were collected and weighed.

choices.label: D
choices.content: It explains the mechanism behind the sinking asserted in the opening sentence.

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: River water carrying clay meets salt water part way down an estuary. In fresh water the clay particles carry like charges and repel one another, so they stay in suspension; in salt water the charges are neutralised and the particles clump into flocs heavy enough to sink. The mud therefore drops out along a band that shifts up and down the estuary with the tide and the river's flow, and the dredgers keep returning to the same few miles of channel year after year.

choices.label: A
choices.content: To compare the clay carried by two different rivers.

choices.label: B
choices.content: To explain why mud settles along one stretch of an estuary rather than throughout it.

choices.label: C
choices.content: To describe the equipment used to dredge a shipping channel.

choices.label: D
choices.content: To argue that dredging an estuary channel is a waste of money.

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A knapper works a lump of obsidian into a fluted cylinder and then presses blades from it one after another, each running the whole length of the core. Sixty or more usable blades can come from a core the size of a fist, and every cutting edge is a fracture surface a few molecules thick. The same edge is brittle: it dulls after a short use, and it cannot be sharpened again, only struck off and replaced.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Pressing blades from a prepared core yields many extremely sharp edges from little stone, but each edge is short-lived.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Obsidian was valued chiefly because its tools could be resharpened many times over.

choices.label: C
choices.content: A core the size of a fist was more than most households could obtain.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The sharpness of an obsidian edge depends on the strength of the knapper.

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Rain falling on cool upland with poor drainage keeps the ground saturated, and the moss that dies beneath the living surface does not rot but accumulates. The peat that builds up holds many times its own weight in water and releases it slowly, so the waterlogging that began the process is afterwards maintained by the peat itself. A bog of this kind is not confined to hollows: it can climb a slope and carry on over the watershed.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Drainage on upland ground improves as the peat above it thickens.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Peat sustains the wet conditions that formed it, which is why such a bog is not restricted to low ground.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Bogs of this kind form only where standing water collects in hollows.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Moss grows more quickly on a slope than it does on level ground.

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Beaudry's argument?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A saltmarsh gains height as each tide leaves a film of sediment on it, and it loses height as the sea rises against it. Ecologist Tomas Beaudry argues that whether a marsh keeps its position relative to the tide depends on how much sediment the estuary delivers to it, not on how vigorously its plants grow.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Marsh plants grow taller on the parts of a marsh that are flooded least often.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The plants of the two estuaries belong to the same species and flower at the same time.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Sediment settles more readily on a marsh surface than on the bare flat in front of it.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Marshes on an estuary whose river was dammed in 1960 fell relative to the tide over the next thirty years, while marshes on a neighbouring undammed estuary rose over the same period.

questions.stem: Which quotation from the report most effectively illustrates Ellery's claim?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: In 1846 a surveyor reported to the owners of a tide mill standing at the head of a creek. Historian Marta Ellery argues that the report was written to show the owners that the mill's working hours were fixed by the tide and could not be lengthened by any improvement to the machinery.

choices.label: A
choices.content: “The stones are of French burr and were dressed within the twelvemonth.”

choices.label: B
choices.content: “A new pair of gates, with the ironwork, would stand the owners in some ninety pounds.”

choices.label: C
choices.content: “The corn brought to this mill comes chiefly from farms lying within four miles of it.”

choices.label: D
choices.content: “The wheel turns while the pond empties and no longer, and at the neaps that period is shorter by an hour whatever gearing be put behind it.”

questions.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
Water enters a soil no faster than its pores allow, and a soil packed tight by traffic has fewer pores open to take it. Four fields on the same soil series, differing only in how heavily they had been worked, were tested for bulk density and for the rate at which water soaked in. Local rainfall reaches 20 millimetres in an hour in the heaviest summer storms.
FieldBulk density (g/cm³)Infiltration rate (mm/hour)
Barn Close1.626
Long Meadow1.4514
Coldharbour1.2831
Slade1.519
Only one of the four fields could take in the heaviest hourly rainfall as fast as it fell, namely _____

choices.label: A
choices.content: Slade, whose bulk density of 1.51 grams per cubic centimetre was below that of Barn Close.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Barn Close, whose infiltration rate of 6 millimetres an hour was the lowest measured.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Coldharbour, whose infiltration rate of 31 millimetres an hour was the only one above 20.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Long Meadow, whose infiltration rate was 14 millimetres an hour.

questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Ammonium carries a positive charge, and the clay and humus of a soil carry negative ones, so ammonium is held on the surfaces it meets and travels very little. Soil bacteria convert ammonium into nitrate within days in warm, moist ground, and nitrate carries a negative charge that nothing in the soil attracts. A field given its nitrogen in autumn rather than in spring is therefore likely to _____

choices.label: A
choices.content: lose a larger share of it to the water draining out of the soil over the winter.

choices.label: B
choices.content: retain a larger share of it, because cool soil converts ammonium more quickly.

choices.label: C
choices.content: hold the nitrogen in place until the crop begins to grow in the spring.

choices.label: D
choices.content: need a heavier application of lime before the crop can take the nitrogen up.

questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Two marsh plants divide the shore between them. One holds the low marsh, which is covered by every tide; the other holds the high marsh, which is covered a few times a month. Moved down into the low marsh, the high-marsh plant dies within a season. Moved up into the high marsh, the low-marsh plant grows perfectly well so long as its neighbour is cut away, and is crowded out within two years if it is not. The evidence indicates that _____

choices.label: A
choices.content: both plants would spread across the whole marsh if the tide were excluded from it.

choices.label: B
choices.content: the lower plant is held down by competition and the upper plant by its tolerance of flooding.

choices.label: C
choices.content: each plant grows only where its own tolerance permits, competition playing no part.

choices.label: D
choices.content: the lower plant grows faster than the upper plant wherever the two are found together.

questions.passage: Willow cut in winter is graded before anything is made from it, and a basketmaker will run a whole bolt through the hand before choosing. The longest _____ kept back for the uprights, which have to carry the shape of the basket from the base to the rim without kinking.

choices.label: B
choices.content: rods those over five feet are

choices.content: rods, those over five feet are

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Teotihuacan was laid out on a grid before most of the city standing on it existed, and the grid was held to for centuries afterwards. The _____ along its side streets housed groups far larger than a single family, each compound with its own courtyard, its own drains and its own small shrine.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A sea lamprey passes its first years buried in river silt as a blind, toothless larva, straining fine particles out of the water above it. Only after it changes _____ does it grow the sucking disc and the rasping tongue with which the adult feeds on other fish.

choices.label: A

choices.content: — a transformation that can take a year,

choices.content: a transformation that can take a year

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A clay tablet from Ugarit, scratched about 1400 BCE, lists thirty signs in a fixed order and nothing else. The order is not the order of anything in the world, and it is not alphabetical in any sense the signs themselves could supply. It is nonetheless the order our own alphabet still runs _____ list of signs was already being recited and learned by heart as a sequence.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A wader that has just crossed an ocean cannot be followed to its feeding grounds, but it can be weighed. The team works the high-tide roost with mist nets, takes each bird's mass to the gram and lets it go within the hour, and the same flock is caught again eleven days later. Caught at the roost and weighed before release, _____

choices.label: A
choices.content: it was found that a third of their arrival mass had been gained in eleven days.

choices.label: B
choices.content: a gain of a third of their arrival mass had taken eleven days.

choices.label: C
choices.content: the birds had gained a third of their arrival mass in eleven days.

choices.label: D
choices.content: eleven days had been enough for a gain of a third of their arrival mass.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The mill at the bridge had ground on two pairs of stones since 1780, and it had taken the corn of six parishes. By the time the roller plant opened in the valley in 1889, the trade in stone-ground flour _____ already begun to fall away.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The charcoal burner sleeps beside the stack for the whole of the burn, and a stack left unwatched for two hours can be lost. Each of the vents cut around the base of the clamp _____ opened and stopped again by hand as the smoke changes colour.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The sacbeob are raised limestone roads, plastered white and in places ten metres across, and some run twenty miles from one centre to another. They were built in a country that had no wheeled vehicles and no pack animals, so everything moving along them moved on somebody's back. _____ they were made wide, level and hard enough to carry traffic of a kind that did not exist.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Peat lifted from the bank is two-thirds water by weight, and a wet turf will not take a flame at all. The cutter stacks the turves in open lattices with the wind blowing through them, turns the stack twice before autumn and carts it home only when it rings under the hand. _____ a fuel that costs nothing to buy costs a summer of work before it will burn.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Soil organisms respond both to temperature and to how much water fills the pores between the grains, and neither factor on its own predicts what a soil will do. _____ a warm soil that is saturated gives off less carbon dioxide than a cool one that is merely damp, because the organisms in the wet soil are short of oxygen.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain how a single standard was made to reach an individual trader's measure. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Local measures varied from town to town across the kingdom.
  • From 1497 bronze standards were sent out to the market towns from the Exchequer.
  • Market officers compared the traders' measures against the town's bronze standard.
  • A measure that matched was stamped, and an unstamped measure could be seized.
  • The bronze standards were themselves copied from a single set kept in London.

choices.label: A
choices.content: From 1497 bronze standards were sent out to the market towns.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Local measures varied from town to town across the kingdom.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The bronze standards were copied from a single set kept in London.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Copies of one London set were sent to the market towns, where officers compared each trader's measure against them and stamped the ones that matched.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain why lime mortar is described as returning to the rock it came from. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Limestone is burned in a kiln, which drives carbon dioxide out of it and leaves quicklime.
  • Water added to quicklime slakes it into a putty.
  • Mortar made from the putty sets by taking carbon dioxide back out of the air.
  • The set material is calcium carbonate, the substance the limestone was made of.
  • A lime mortar goes on hardening for years as the change works inward from the surface.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Limestone is burned in a kiln, which drives carbon dioxide out of it.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Burning drives carbon dioxide out of the limestone and the set takes it back from the air, leaving the mortar as the same carbonate the stone was.

choices.label: C
choices.content: A lime mortar goes on hardening for years after it is laid.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Water added to quicklime slakes it into a putty.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain why Maya dates can be placed more precisely than those of neighbouring cultures. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Maya monuments carry dates counted in days from a fixed starting point in 3114 BCE.
  • The count runs continuously and does not restart with a new ruler.
  • Neighbouring cultures dated events by the reign in which they fell.
  • A Long Count date can be placed to the individual day.
  • Fixing the whole count against the European calendar took scholars several decades.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Fixing the count against the European calendar took scholars several decades.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Maya monuments carry dates counted in days from a fixed starting point.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Because the Maya count runs in days from one fixed point and does not restart with each ruler, a date can be placed to the day, while neighbouring cultures dated events by reign.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Neighbouring cultures dated events by the reign in which they fell.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A cob wall is raised from a stiff mixture of subsoil, straw and water thrown up in courses about half a metre high. Each course must dry and take its own weight before the next can go on, and the sides are pared back with a spade once they are firm. A wall of any height therefore takes a season and cannot be hurried, so building in cob is necessarily _____.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Limewash is slaked lime thinned with water and brushed on in coats so thin that the wall shows through the first of them. It shuts nothing in: damp reaching the face of a limewashed wall passes out through the coating and dries, so no water is trapped behind a skin. A fresh coat costs the price of the lime and a morning of somebody's time. Its virtue is not that it lasts but that it is so easily _____.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A thatched roof is not sealed. Water reed is laid in overlapping courses with the cut butts facing outward, and rain that strikes the surface runs down the outside of the stems and off the eaves without passing more than a few centimetres into the coat. The pitch matters more than the depth, because a shallow roof lets the water travel along the stems instead of down them: the covering works by _____ the rain rather than by blocking it.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A hide is moved through a series of pits, each holding a stronger liquor of crushed oak bark than the last, and a year may pass before it comes out. A tanner who hurries the sequence fixes the outer faces of the hide before the liquor has reached the middle, and the leather cracks along the fold. The slowness of the older pits was therefore _____ rather than a mark of an industry that had not yet been improved.

questions.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “charge” most nearly mean?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A lime kiln is loaded from the top in alternating layers: a bed of coal, then broken limestone, then coal again, until the shaft is full. The burner draws quicklime from the grate at the bottom as the column settles and adds another <u>charge</u> at the top, so that the kiln runs for months without being emptied or allowed to cool.

questions.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Stones grind the whole grain at once, so the oil of the germ is smeared through the meal and the flour turns rancid within weeks. <u>Rollers set in pairs and turned at different speeds shear each grain open instead of crushing it, so that bran and germ come away in flakes large enough to be sifted out whole.</u> The flour that resulted was white, kept for months and could be sent anywhere, and the country mills lost the trade within a generation.

choices.label: A
choices.content: It identifies the change in method that accounts for the qualities described afterwards.

choices.label: B
choices.content: It concedes that stone-ground flour had advantages the new method lacked.

choices.label: C
choices.content: It explains why the germ of the grain contains oil.

choices.label: D
choices.content: It estimates how quickly the country mills lost their trade.

questions.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A plank walkway laid across a reed swamp about 3800 BCE survives beneath a Somerset peat field. <u>Its builders drove pairs of pegs into the swamp in a long crossed line, dropped a rail into the notch where each pair crossed, and pegged the planks down onto the rail.</u> Nothing in the structure rested on the surface itself. The result carried people in single file above ground that would not have held a standing adult.

choices.label: A
choices.content: It establishes the date at which the walkway was built.

choices.label: B
choices.content: It accounts for the survival of the timbers in the peat.

choices.label: C
choices.content: It compares the walkway with roads built later in the same region.

choices.label: D
choices.content: It sets out the arrangement whose purpose the rest of the text explains.

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The signs of the earliest alphabet are pictures: an ox head, a house, a door. Each sign stands not for the thing drawn but for the sound that opens the word naming it, so the ox head writes the first sound of the word for ox. Twenty-odd signs used this way covered a language that would have needed several hundred to be written word by word, and a list that short could be learned in days by people who were not scribes by trade.

choices.label: A
choices.content: An alphabet of twenty-odd signs cannot represent every sound of a language.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Letting each picture stand for the first sound of its own name cut writing down to a couple of dozen signs.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The pictures were chosen because they were the easiest shapes to draw.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Scribes resisted the new signs because the older system suited them better.

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: An acre began as a day's work rather than a quantity of ground: the strip a man with a yoke of oxen could plough between morning and evening. Its size therefore moved with the soil, and a heavy clay acre was a good deal smaller than an acre of light loam. The unit told a farmer the one thing he needed, which was how long a field would take him. It told a purchaser at a distance nothing whatever about how much ground he was buying.

choices.label: A
choices.content: The acre was abandoned once oxen were replaced by horses at the plough.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Farmers preferred light loam because it could be ploughed into larger fields.

choices.label: C
choices.content: A unit defined by a day's labour reported effort accurately and area only loosely.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Ploughmen working heavy clay were less productive than those working light loam.

questions.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:

choices.label: B

choices.label: C
choices.content: Denton, whose bushel held exactly 35.2 litres.

choices.label: D

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Achebe's argument?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: In a few arable fields a root disease that is present in the soil nevertheless fails to damage the crop, and the fields keep this property for decades. Soil scientist Wren Achebe argues that the suppression is the work of living organisms in the soil rather than of its chemistry.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Heating a suppressive soil destroys the suppression, and mixing one part of untreated soil into fifty parts of the heated soil restores it.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Suppressive fields hold more organic matter than neighbouring fields that lack the property.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The disease damages crops most severely in warm, wet seasons.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Suppressive soils have been recorded on several continents and in several soil types.

questions.stem: Which quotation from the notebook most effectively illustrates Rask's claim?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Between 1936 and 1939 an amateur excavator kept a notebook while a ditch was deepened along the edge of a fen, where rows of oak piles kept appearing in the cut. Archaeologist Nils Rask argues that the notebook shows its author satisfying himself that the piles were the footings of a built structure some two years before he could persuade anyone else of it.

choices.label: A
choices.content: “They stand four abreast and at even spacing, and no flood I can picture would set them so; I take them for the footings of something raised above the water.”

choices.label: B
choices.content: “The ditch was opened to a depth of five feet and the spoil laid along the western bank.”

choices.label: C
choices.content: “Mr Ridley of the Manor Farm allows that we may work the field until Michaelmas next year.”

choices.label: D
choices.content: “Two of the piles were sawn through at the waterline and the sections carried to the county museum.”

questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Egyptian inscriptions run left to right in some places and right to left in others, and a single wall may carry lines of both kinds. The signs themselves settle the question: the human and animal figures always face towards the start of the line, so a row of owls and seated men looking leftward is to be read from the left. A reader who has never seen a particular inscription before can therefore _____

choices.label: A
choices.content: translate the inscription without knowing anything of the language it records.

choices.label: B
choices.content: date the inscription by the direction in which its lines were cut.

choices.label: C
choices.content: tell which of the figures the inscription was composed to honour.

choices.label: D
choices.content: work out which end of each line to begin at from the direction the figures face.

questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Tannin enters a hide slowly, working inward from both faces at once, and a hide lifted too early looks finished from the outside. A tanner therefore cuts a narrow strip from the edge of a hide and examines the cut end: where the liquor has done its work the section is brown throughout, and where it has not an untanned core shows as a pale line down the middle. A pale line in the sample tells the tanner that _____

choices.label: A
choices.content: the hide was cut from an animal too young to yield usable leather.

choices.label: B
choices.content: the sample was taken from the wrong part of the hide and must be cut again.

choices.label: C
choices.content: the hide must go back into the pits, since the liquor has not yet reached its centre.

choices.label: D
choices.content: the liquor was too strong and has scorched the outer faces of the hide.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain how one piece of ground could yield two things at once. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • A pollard is a tree cut back to a permanent trunk two or three metres above the ground.
  • The height of the cut puts the regrowth out of reach of cattle and deer.
  • Wood pasture carries grazing animals and a wood crop on the same ground.
  • A tree that is cut in this way regularly can go on producing for several centuries.
  • The cut poles were used for fuel, fencing and tool handles.

choices.label: A
choices.content: A tree cut in this way regularly can go on producing for several centuries.

choices.label: B
choices.content: A pollard is a tree cut back to a permanent trunk above the ground.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The cut poles were used for fuel, fencing and tool handles.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Cutting above the height cattle and deer can reach keeps the regrowth safe from them, so the same ground carries grazing animals and a wood crop together.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain why the ridge is dealt with separately from the rest of the roof. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • The ridge of a thatched roof takes more weather than the slopes below it.
  • A ridge is renewed every ten to fifteen years.
  • A full re-coat of the slopes is needed only every twenty-five to sixty years, depending on the material.
  • Re-ridging requires a few days of work and one bundle of sedge in ten of the coat.
  • The ridge is fixed with hazel spars and can be stripped without disturbing the coat beneath it.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Because the ridge wears out several times over during the life of the coat and can be stripped without disturbing it, it is renewed on its own in a few days.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Re-ridging requires one bundle of sedge in every ten of the coat.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The ridge of a thatched roof takes more weather than the slopes below it.

choices.label: D
choices.content: A ridge is renewed every ten to fifteen years.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain why a millwright would go to the expense of digging a leat. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • An undershot wheel is turned by water striking the paddles at the bottom of the wheel.
  • An overshot wheel is turned by the weight of water carried down in buckets from the top.
  • An overshot wheel needs a head of water at least as high as the wheel itself.
  • Building a leat along the contour can carry water from far upstream to the top of a wheel.
  • For the same flow, an overshot wheel yields roughly twice the power of an undershot one.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Building a leat along the contour can carry water from far upstream.

choices.label: B
choices.content: An undershot wheel is turned by water striking its paddles at the bottom.

choices.label: C
choices.content: A leat carried along the contour delivers water at the height an overshot wheel needs, and such a wheel yields about twice the power of an undershot one on the same flow.

choices.label: D
choices.content: An overshot wheel is turned by the weight of water carried down in buckets.

questions.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “standard” most nearly mean?

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Six species of wader feed on one mudflat at the same tide. Their bills run from the two-centimetre probe of a stint to the twelve-centimetre curve of a curlew, and the animals buried in the mud are arranged by depth: small snails and thin worms near the surface, thick worms and burrowing crabs well below. Records of what each species swallows show almost no overlap at all between the shortest bills and the longest.

choices.label: A
choices.content: To explain how species feeding on the same ground take different prey from it.

choices.label: B
choices.content: To argue that curlews drive smaller waders off the flats they share.

choices.label: C
choices.content: To describe how the animals buried in a mudflat construct their burrows.

choices.label: D
choices.content: To establish which of the six species is the most numerous on the flat.

questions.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

questions.passage: <u>A Maya vault is built by setting each course of stone a little further out than the course below until the two sides almost meet, and closing the gap with a capstone.</u> Nothing in the structure carries a load sideways, so the walls must be thick enough to hold the overhang up by sheer weight. choices.label: A
choices.content: It explains why the capstone is the heaviest element in the roof.

choices.label: B
choices.content: It states how tall the rooms roofed in this way could be made.

choices.label: C

choices.label: D

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A lime mortar is weaker than the brick or stone it beds, and that is the point of it. As a wall moves, the fine cracks open along the joints rather than through the units, and a joint is the one part of a wall a mason can rake out and replace. A cement mortar is much stronger and much stiffer, and in a wall of soft brick the crack runs through the brick instead. Repointing an old soft wall in cement can leave it worse than it was.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Cement mortar cracks more readily than lime mortar does.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Soft bricks should be replaced with harder ones before a wall is repointed.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The chief advantage of lime mortar is that it costs less than cement.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Mortar weaker than the masonry sends damage into the joints, where it can be repaired, which is why cement can harm a soft old wall.

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Two constructions account for nearly every basket ever made. In the first, a bundle of grass or straw is wound in a rising spiral and each turn is stitched to the one below it, so the wall grows by sewing. In the second, stout rods are set upright as a framework and finer rods are woven in and out between them, so the wall grows by weaving. The first needs a needle and almost no strength; the second needs rods that bend without cracking and a maker who can hold them under strain.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Both methods were developed in order to make use of grass and straw.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Basketmakers generally learn the woven method before attempting the coiled one.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The two methods build a wall in different ways and therefore ask different things of the maker's material and tools.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Coiled baskets are stronger than woven ones and last considerably longer.

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Sørensen's argument?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Salmon hatched in a small tributary return years later to the same tributary, choosing correctly at every fork on the way up. Biologist Ingrid Sørensen argues that the fish make those choices by smell, having learned the odour of their own stream before they went to sea.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Young salmon spend between one and three years in fresh water before going to sea.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The two branches of the confluence differ in temperature by about one degree in summer.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Adults whose nostrils were plugged turned into the two branches of a confluence at random, while untagged fish from the same run turned overwhelmingly into their natal branch.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Salmon return to the river in greater numbers in years when the autumn flow is high.

questions.stem: Which quotation from the letter book most effectively illustrates Larkin's claim?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The letter book of a Munster tannery covers the years 1783 to 1791, and its entries record purchases, wages and the state of the pits alongside the partners' correspondence with their agents in Cork and Bristol. Historian Aoife Larkin argues that what governed the firm's output in those years was its supply of oak bark rather than its supply of hides.

choices.content: “We have taken on two men for the beam house and shall want a third before spring.”

choices.label: B
choices.content: “Hides we may have out of Cork whenever we send for them; it is the bark that settles how many pits we dare lay down.”

choices.label: C
choices.content: “The new pits behind the drying loft were finished at Michaelmas and are of the same depth as the old.”

choices.label: D
choices.content: “Sole leather is fetching a better price this season than at any time since the war.”

questions.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
Knots feeding on an estuary before their northward flight are caught, weighed and released. A team recorded the mean mass of the birds caught in the week of their arrival and again in the week before they left, at four estuaries in the same spring.

choices.label: B
choices.content: had to carry the whole of its fuel from the start, being in no condition to feed on the way.

choices.content: fed on small animals taken from the surface of the sea during the crossing.

questions.passage: When a peat fen is drained the peat dries, shrinks and wastes away as air reaches it. choices.label: A
choices.content: a measure of how far the surface of the fen has fallen since the drainage.

choices.label: B
choices.content: evidence that the clay beneath the peat has been pushed slowly upward.

choices.label: C
choices.content: a record of the height reached by the water in the drain beside it.

choices.label: D
choices.content: proof that the wasting of the peat has now come to an end.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain how blocking the ditches changes what a drained bog does. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Peat forms only while the ground stays waterlogged, and it wastes away once air reaches it.
  • A drained peat field loses several millimetres of its surface every year.
  • Blocking the ditches on a drained bog raises the water table back to within a few centimetres of the surface.
  • Sphagnum moss returns to the wetted surface within a few seasons.
  • Gas measurements on rewetted bogs record far less carbon dioxide leaving the ground than before the ditches were blocked.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Blocking the ditches raises the water table to within a few centimetres of the surface, and gas measurements then record far less carbon dioxide leaving the ground.

choices.label: B
choices.content: A drained peat field loses several millimetres of its surface every year.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Peat forms only while the ground stays waterlogged.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Sphagnum moss returns to a rewetted surface within a few seasons.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain why parchment is not a kind of leather. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Tanning binds tannin into the fibres of a hide, and a tanned hide never returns to its raw state.
  • Parchment is made by liming a skin, scraping it and drying it under tension; no tannin is used at all.
  • Parchment that is wetted relaxes, shrinks and cockles as it dries again.
  • A tanned hide that is wetted dries flat and unchanged.
  • Parchment and leather are both made from animal skin.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Parchment and leather are both made from animal skin.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Parchment is dried under tension without tannin, so wetting relaxes and cockles it, whereas a tanned hide dries flat and unchanged.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Parchment is made by liming a skin and then scraping it.

choices.label: D
choices.content: A tanned hide never returns to its raw state once the tannin is in the fibres.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain how breaching the old wall changed the life of the site. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • The marsh in front of the wall narrowed as the sea rose against it.

choices.content: Letting the tide back through the breach allowed glasswort to colonise the bare mud within two seasons, and counts of feeding waders on the site rose sharply afterwards.

choices.label: B
choices.content: A new wall was built further inland in 2002.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The marsh in front of the old wall narrowed as the sea rose against it.

choices.label: D
choices.content: A sea wall built across the estuary in 1850 cut off two hundred hectares from the tide.
